Quotation software in Malaysia: QCON vs Excel vs accounting software

Updated 11 November 2026

Most Malaysian contractors and interior designers quote in one of three ways: an Excel or Google Sheets template, the quotation module of their accounting software, or a tool built for quotations. Excel is free but error-prone once a job has many lines and revisions. Accounting software is great for invoices and e-invoicing but treats quotes as a simple item list. A contractor quotation tool like QCON adds what renovation work needs: sections by trade, and cost vs selling price with your margin on every line.

When Excel is enough

If you send a few quotations a month with a short list of items, a good spreadsheet works. Start from a template with formulas already in place, such as our free renovation quotation template, and always export to PDF before sending so the client can't change your figures.

Excel starts costing you money when:

  • a scope change means re-checking formulas across dozens of lines;
  • you can't tell which version the client saw;
  • you only find out after the job that a line was priced below cost.

When accounting software makes sense

You need accounting software anyway for invoices, payments, SST and, if your sales are above RM3 million a year, e-invoicing through LHDN's MyInvois. Its quotation module is convenient when your quotes are simple and turn straight into invoices. It's less suited to renovation and fit-out quotes, where you group work by trade, track what each item costs you, and revise the quote several times before the client signs.

When a contractor quotation tool like QCON fits

  • You quote multi-trade jobs (hacking, tiling, carpentry, electrical, plumbing, painting) and want each section clearly subtotalled.
  • You need to see your margin before you send. QCON keeps your cost and your selling price on every line, so underquoting shows up immediately.
  • You revise quotes often. Duplicate a past job, adjust it, and keep every quotation in one list instead of scattered files.
  • Your team quotes too. Admins and staff work from the same company details, logo and terms.

QCON is not accounting software. It handles the quotation stage, and once the job is confirmed you invoice in your existing system. Many contractors use both.

Checklist: what to look for in quotation software

  1. Sections or categories by trade, with subtotals
  2. Unit, quantity and rate on every line (sq ft, ft run, point, lot)
  3. Your cost and selling price per line, with the margin shown
  4. Discount, tax and payment terms
  5. A validity period on every quote
  6. A clean PDF with your logo and SSM number
  7. Fast revisions: duplicate and edit instead of starting again
  8. A free plan or trial so you can test it on a real job

Do quotations need e-invoicing?

No. E-invoicing applies to invoices, not quotations. Since 1 September 2026, businesses with annual sales below RM3 million are exempt from e-invoicing, though LHDN still encourages voluntary adoption. If you do issue e-invoices, keep doing that in your accounting software. Your quotation tool doesn't need to handle it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best quotation software for contractors in Malaysia?
It depends on what you need. If you already use accounting software and only send simple quotes, its quotation module may be enough. If you price renovation or fit-out jobs with many trades and need to see cost, selling price and margin on every line, a quotation tool built for contractors, such as QCON, saves time and prevents underquoting. Excel works for occasional, simple quotes.
Do I need e-invoicing for quotations in Malaysia?
No. A quotation is not an invoice, so it is not submitted to LHDN's MyInvois system. E-invoicing applies to invoices, and since 1 September 2026 businesses with annual sales below RM3 million are exempt. If you issue e-invoices, do that in your accounting software, and use a quotation tool for the quotes that come before.
Can I use QCON together with my accounting software?
Yes. QCON handles the quotation stage (pricing, margins, revisions and the PDF your client signs). Once the job is confirmed, you invoice and do your accounts in your existing accounting software.
Is Excel good enough for renovation quotations?
For a few simple quotes, yes. It gets risky with many line items and revisions: a broken formula, a missed line or sending the wrong version can cost you the job's margin. Use a template with locked formulas, or move to a dedicated tool when you quote regularly.
Is QCON free?
QCON has a free plan for occasional use, and new accounts start with a free Pro trial without a credit card. Pro removes the monthly quotation limit and adds team members.
